crossRefs.note: When he had agreed with the laborers for a denarius a day, he sent them into his vineyard.
Gaius, my host and host of the whole assembly, greets you. Erastus, the treasurer of the city, greets you, as does…
But when you make a feast, ask the poor, the maimed, the lame, or the blind;
He who has pity on the poor lends to Yahweh; he will reward him.

translations.web: On the next day, when he departed, he took out two denarii, gave them to the host, and said to him, ‘Take care of him. Whatever you spend beyond that, I will repay you when I return.’
translations.bsb: The next day he took out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper. ‘Take care of him,’ he said, ‘and on my return I will repay you for any additional expense.’
translations.kjv: And on the morrow when he departed, he took out two pence, and gave them to the host, and said unto him, Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, when I come again, I will repay thee.
translations.asv: And on the morrow he took out two shillings, and gave them to the host, and said, Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, I, when I come back again, will repay thee.
